## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- Text becomes a sequence of tokens. An autoregressive LLM predicts the next token from the tokens already in its context.
- A forward pass turns that context into scores. The scores at the last position can then be normalized into a distribution over the vocabulary.
- Generation selects a token and feeds it back into the context. Training uses known targets to adjust the parameters. During generation, the parameters stay fixed.
- Parameters encode learned patterns. The context provides the current instructions and examples. The same prediction task can support summarization or translation depending on that context.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

What changes when a token is appended during generation?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

The context grows by one token. The network parameters stay fixed. The next distribution depends on the updated context.

</details>
